quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel lively and confident after drinking. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, reduces your coordination and balance, and makes it harder to judge distances and react to your surroundings.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to not drink alcohol and let time pass. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers can keep you awake, but they cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: When you see railroad tracks ahead, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same before you start the engine.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from serious injury or death while driving.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit, you should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Keep driving until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up or try to turn around. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway is illegal.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Assume no train is coming and keep driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be near. Always follow these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: On highways, you must stay alert and keep your eyes moving. Look away from any one spot for no more than a few seconds. Be ready to react to unexpected dangers.

questions.question: How far your car travels before stopping depends on:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: When you see another driver acting angry, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When another driver is angry, avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move over, and stay away from them to keep yourself safe.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, you should:

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Yield to all vehicles already on the highway.
Turn on headlights and drive quickly without yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to all vehicles already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from a driveway or private road, yield to all traffic already on the highway. Enter only when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move away from that driver.
Flash your lights to show the driver is wrong.
Drive aggressively back at that driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move away from that driver.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get revenge makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in these situations:

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer signals you to stop.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop to let them cross safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the intersection. Protect pedestrians no matter what the traffic light says.

questions.question: The sign with this shape and color is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs only mark no passing zones.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should skip their stop.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.
